title: Zero-to-Call Hosted API Playbook
content:
Goal: produce a compact, actionable playbook that marketing, growth, and docs can use to convert devs from curiosity -> API call within 10 minutes. Focus: developer-first value props, three quickstart angles, and two pricing language drafts (metered & commit).

Executive summary:
- Problem: Developers abandon trial because the first call feels heavy (key setup, vague UX, unclear cost signal).
- Our hypothesis: a 3-step onramp (one-line import, sample request, visible cost preview) + dev-centric copy reduces time-to-first-call and increases trial->paid conversion.
- Primary metrics: time-to-first-successful-response, CTA conversion on quickstart page, average tokens on first 24h.

Positioning pillars (short, repeatable):
1) Engineered for production speed — predictable latency at scale so prototypes don't need to be rewritten.
2) Dev ergonomics first — tiny SDKs, curated starter prompts, local mocks for CI.
3) Cost clarity — preflight cost estimate, easy switching between performance/cost variants.

Plain-language value props (for pages, emails, docs):
- "Get a response in under 50ms — real numbers you can rely on in prod."
- "Ship conversational features without rewriting when you scale."
- "Free dev tier, then per-token metering; switch to committed capacity when you need predictable throughput."

Three quickstart angles (copy + callouts):
1) Curl-first (fastest path for curious devs)
- One-sentence intro: "Try a model in <2 minutes with curl — no SDK install required."
- Steps: create key (1 click), paste curl, see JSON, copy snippet into bash.
- Callouts: show sample input, sample output, estimated token cost for request.
- Objection handled: "I don't want secrets in shell" -> recommend ephemeral keys and command that uses env var.

2) JS SDK (most strategic for product devs)
- One-sentence intro: "Add 3 lines of code and get streaming responses into your app."
- Minimal snippet: import client, call generate, stream to UI.
- Add optional: local mock server cmd to run tests offline.
- Callouts: highlight small package size, tree-shakeable imports, examples for React + Next.js.

3) CI / E2E safe test (enterprise & SRE comfort)
- One-sentence intro: "Run a smoke test in CI with a free test key that never bills."
- Steps: install redwood-cli, run redwood test-call, assert 200.
- Callouts: show how to pin model version in test to avoid drift; link to rollout docs.

Developer copy snippets (for landing, button text, CTAs):
- Landing header: "Build fast. Ship predictable."
- Subheader: "Hosted LLM inference for dev teams that treat latency and cost like first-class citizens."
- Primary CTA: "Try a request — no signup" (leads to ephemeral auth popup)
- Secondary CTA: "Start a free project" (creates dashboard + credit).

Pricing-language drafts (two variants)
A) Metered-first (simple, low-friction)
- Consumer-facing blurb: "Free tier: 100k tokens / month. After that, pay-as-you-go by token with per-model rates. No minimums."
- Key advantage: low risk to try.
- How to display on quickstart: show inline estimator beneath sample request: "This request ≈ 12 tokens (~$0.00012)".
- Risk: noisy cost spikes for high-throughput tests. Mitigation: default rate limit on new keys + in-dashboard cost alerts.

B) Commit-first (apply for larger customers)
- Blurb: "Committed capacity for predictable throughput & lower unit costs. Monthly reservations, burstable headroom, SLA options."
- Sales hook: propose savings example (50M tokens/month saves ~40% vs metered).
- How to surface: product page, pricing calc, dedicated signup for enterprise trials.

Sample pricing microcopy (short)
- Metered: "Free 100k tokens / mo. After that, $X per 1k tokens for standard models."
- Committed: "Reserved pools, SLA, discounted unit pricing — talk to sales."

Competitive notes — quick hits (for KM and enablement)
- Large cloud AI platforms: pros: integrated infra, single bill; cons: variable latency at scale, less tuned quantization recommendations.
- LLM API providers (simplicity-focused): pros: easy to use; cons: opaque performance metrics, weak rollout tooling.
- Self-hosted runtimes: pros: max control; cons: high ops burden, slow to iterate.
- Our angle: balance low friction with production-grade controls (observable latency, rollouts, fallback).

Objections & rebuttals (sales/dev-rel scripts)
- "I need private deployment": "We offer Redwood Private for VPC and on-prem; start on hosted to prototype then flip the control plane when ready."
- "I care about cost — how do I avoid surprises?": "We show per-request estimates, set sensible default limits on new keys, and provide Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization."
- "Will it break when I scale?": "Predictable latency SLOs, dedicated capacity plans, and automatic model fallbacks keep your app online."

Call-to-action experiments to test (A/B ideas)
- CTA text A: "Try a request — no signup" vs CTA B: "Start a free project" (measure signup funnel).
- Quickstart A: show token estimator inline vs Quickstart B: show cost only at checkout.
- Onboarding A: ephemeral keys + sample curl vs B: guided tour with code editor embed.

Tracking plan (minimum events)
- quickstart_page_view, quickstart_start_method (curl/js/ci), first_successful_response_time, ephemeral_key_created, billing_estimator_clicked, signup_after_quickstart.

One-line email sequences for trial nudge (day 1 / day 3 / day 7)
- Day 1 subject: "Your first API call — quick steps (2 mins)"
  body: quick curl snippet + link to estimator + "Need a code sample? Reply and we'll send a tailored example."
- Day 3 subject: "How to keep costs low while you test"
  body: tips: small context windows, batching, free dev tier reminder + link to Optimize suggestions.

Next steps (action items):
- Growth: implement CTA A/B test on quickstart landing (owner: Liam Chen) — 2-week experiment.
- Docs: add ephemeral key flow + inline token estimator to curl and JS quickstarts (owner: Priya).
- Product: default new keys to soft-rate-limit + in-dashboard alerts (owner: Jonas).
- Sales: create short one-pager for commit vs metered economics (owner: Evelyn).

Appendix: tactical copy examples (paste-ready)
- Hero alternative: "Inference that scales with your product, not your engineering team."
- Microcopy for token estimator tooltip: "Estimate uses median response length for this model. Actual cost may vary."
- Toast after first successful call: "Nice — first call succeeded. This request used ~12 tokens (~$0.00012). Pin this example to your project."

Notes and open questions (raw):
- Should we offer an interactive playground that mints ephemeral keys for public demos? Privacy concerns + abuse mitigation needed.
- What is the exact free tier token count that balances cost exposure and developer freedom? (Modeling required)
- Confirm UX for default rate-limits on new keys and what the in-dashboard alert cadence should be.

Document history: initial draft 2024-09-18 by Asha. Reviewed 2025-07-11 with PMs and Docs.
